label: First copy step (re-reading orig token 0, outputting token 1) in short L=3 sequences that end in f/n and start with k/l-like letters
explanation: Sparse feature (124 sequences). Nearly all activation (98.5%) is at the step right after <DEL>: recall_idx == 1, where the input is the fed-back orig(0) and the model outputs orig(1). It is almost entirely limited to short sequences (L=3 holds 86% of mass, L=4 13%) whose last original token (or for L=4 the next-to-last) is f or n, and whose first token is k or l (about 70% of mass), with y/r/z/p/t/q making up the rest. The strongest examples are l/k _ f/n <DEL> l/k. The middle token also matters: k/l _ f/n sequences with middle o, g, d, s, w, 1 often stay silent, which is why precision is low; I did not find a clean rule for the middle token. It never fires during the original phase (one exception) or at the delimiter, and never at later copy steps or in L >= 5 sequences. The highest values occur with first token l/k and last token f/n; I did not find a clear magnitude trend beyond that. Best dev predicate: F1 0.29, mass recall 0.72.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 22 cues. Raise it: recall_idx=1 & in_tok=k (+2.86), recall_idx=1 & in_tok=l (+2.62), prev2_tok=f (+1.69), orig2=n (+1.35), next_out=f (+1.29), phase=2 & out_tok=f (+1.22). Lower it: in_first=1 (-1.56), n_digits=1 (-1.35).
